rationale: The target is privacy-conscious home users and hobbyists who self-host Nextcloud — a group that overwhelmingly expects free, open-source software and has essentially zero willingness to pay for a niche GUI utility. The buyer is an individual consumer with no budget authority, no existing spend signal, and the solution itself is a native desktop GUI app that cannot be built with Claude prompts or delivered as a service. Operational autonomy is near zero: a desktop app requires per-platform builds, installation support, and ongoing OS compatibility work. Total is well below every threshold.
solution_plan: This is not a viable opportunity for this factory. The audience (self-hosted Linux hobbyists) does not pay for tools of this type, the solution is a native desktop application that Claude cannot build or deliver as a hosted service, and there is no recurring revenue model. A solo non-technical operator cannot build and maintain a cross-platform GUI sync client. Drop entirely.
notes: willingness_to_pay (2), buyer_clarity (3), buildability_with_ai (2), operational_autonomy (2) all fail build gates. Total 2.8 — drop.
